_readme: Accessibility baseline for the axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) e2e gate in a11y.spec.ts. The gate excludes no region of the page, and tolerates a violation only when its node sits inside one of the @dhis2/ui components listed below, matched by axe rule id plus that component's own data-test selector. Anchoring on the component rather than on a page region or an individual element is deliberate: adding a nav entry or another shell element does not turn the gate red for a defect the vendor already owns, yet every other rule on those components, and every rule on the app's own markup wherever it sits, still fails. Note this bounds what is TOLERATED, not what is REACHED — axe only sees the DOM as rendered at that moment, so the spec expands every collapsed section first, and states never exercised (validation errors, calendar overlays, select popovers) stay unaudited. Add an entry only for a defect that is genuinely unfixable from the app, quote the vendor source that causes it, and re-check the list on each @dhis2/ui upgrade.

ignored.note: @dhis2/ui <Menu> renders <ul role="menu"> (menu/menu.js) whose <li> children carry role="presentation" together with a tabindex (menu-item/menu-item.js). A focusable element's presentation role is conflict-resolved back to its implicit role, so the menu's owned children compute as listitem. Structural to the component — it fires for every MenuItem regardless of the props the app passes.
The same @dhis2/ui <Menu> defect seen from the child side: each <a role="menuitem"> sits inside the conflict-resolved <li>, so its parent computes as listitem instead of menu.
@dhis2/ui <HeaderBar> apps-menu toggle (header-bar/apps.js): an icon-only <button> holding just an IconApps24 svg, with no aria-label and no text content.

@dhis2/ui logo link (header-bar/logo.js): wrapping a nameless LogoIconWhite svg. Fires only while the instance has no custom logo banner configured — the custom-logo branch renders an that carries an alt attribute.

@dhis2-ui/header-bar 10.16.0 notification-icon.js: the unread badge is styled `background-color: theme.secondary500; color: colors.white; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600`. secondary500 resolves to colors.teal500 = #00897b, giving 4.32:1 against white where AA wants 4.5:1 — 13px at weight 600 is not WCAG large text, which needs 18.66px bold or 24px. The app cannot reach it: @dhis2/app-adapter's ConnectedHeaderBar passes only appName, the PWA update props and skipI18n, so no colour is ours to set. Note the badge renders only under `count > 0` (notification-icon.js), so a route is green whenever the signed-in user has no unread messages — the gate is quiet by circumstance, not by conformance. The same component draws the interpretations badge from the same rule, so headerbar-interpretations-count fails identically once it carries a count; it is not listed here because it has not been observed failing.
